loci.title: Hereditary Information Intake
loci.micro_anchor: the archive intake where DNA and RNA are filed as hereditary information while the discovery evidence remains contextual rather than becoming the main memorization target

loci.title: Chromosome Storage Gallery
loci.micro_anchor: the storage gallery separating typical prokaryotic circular chromosomes, eukaryotic linear chromosomes, and condensation states

loci.title: Plasmid Ring Vault
loci.micro_anchor: the small-ring vault where plasmids replicate independently, carry conditionally useful genes, and can be engineered or transferred

loci.title: Base-Class Reading Table
loci.micro_anchor: the base table sorting purines and pyrimidines while Chargaff relationships constrain complementary pairing

loci.title: Antiparallel Pairing Bridge
loci.micro_anchor: the double-strand bridge reconnecting 5′/3′ directionality, antiparallel geometry, complementary pairing, and typical DNA/RNA architecture

loci.title: Replication Continuity Gate
loci.micro_anchor: the entry gate linking S phase and DNA copying to hereditary continuity before the fork machinery begins

loci.title: Replication Model Test Chamber
loci.micro_anchor: the evidence chamber comparing conservative, semiconservative, and dispersive predictions against the Meselson–Stahl result

loci.title: Origin and Fork Launch
loci.micro_anchor: the launch platform where replication begins at origins, helicase opens the duplex, topoisomerase relieves twisting, and the fork becomes visible

loci.title: Primer–Polymerase Dock
loci.micro_anchor: the synthesis dock where exposed templates are stabilized, primase supplies RNA primers, and DNA polymerase extends only from a primer in the allowed direction

loci.title: Leading–Lagging Split Track
loci.micro_anchor: the fork track separating continuous leading-strand synthesis from discontinuous lagging-strand synthesis and Okazaki fragments

loci.title: Fragment Joining and Repair Bench
loci.micro_anchor: the post-fork bench where primer replacement is contextual, ligase seals lagging-strand fragments, and proofreading/repair preserve sequence accuracy

loci.title: Chromosome-End Dock
loci.micro_anchor: the chromosome-end dock distinguishing telomeres from telomerase while keeping the detailed end-replication mechanism as enrichment

loci.title: RNA Function Desk
loci.micro_anchor: the RNA desk where sequence and structure are tied to RNA function and mRNA, tRNA, and rRNA receive distinct jobs

loci.title: tRNA Courier Bay
loci.micro_anchor: the courier bay where each tRNA carries a specific amino acid, pairs its anticodon with mRNA, and is recruited during translation

loci.title: Gene Expression Junction
loci.micro_anchor: the junction separating transcription from translation while reactivating protein structure as the downstream functional destination

loci.title: Template–Promoter Entry Gate
loci.micro_anchor: the transcription entry gate where one DNA template strand is distinguished from the opposite strand and promoter/TATA context is placed before transcription begins

loci.title: Transcription Direction Rail
loci.micro_anchor: the rail that locks RNA synthesis direction to the template orientation and carries initiation, elongation, and termination in sequence

loci.title: Prokaryotic Transcript Exit
loci.micro_anchor: the prokaryotic exit showing why a transcript can become usable without the eukaryotic nucleus-based processing route

loci.title: Pre-mRNA Processing Counter
loci.micro_anchor: the eukaryotic processing counter where pre-mRNA receives a 5′ cap and poly-A tail before export

loci.title: Splice and Isoform Chamber
loci.micro_anchor: the chamber where introns are removed, exons are joined, alternative splicing changes exon combinations, and mature mRNA exits

loci.title: Translation Geography Platform
loci.micro_anchor: the platform contrasting eukaryotic translation location with coupled transcription–translation in prokaryotes

loci.title: Reading-Frame Start Gate
loci.micro_anchor: the start gate that establishes a reading frame at AUG and launches the initiation–elongation–termination sequence

loci.title: Codon Code Wall
loci.micro_anchor: the code wall linking triplet codons to amino acids while showing redundancy and near universality without requiring code-table memorization

loci.title: tRNA Charging Dock
loci.micro_anchor: the dock where aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase links the correct amino acid to tRNA before the charged tRNA delivers that amino acid to the ribosome

loci.title: Ribosome A–P–E Platform
loci.micro_anchor: the ribosome platform locating tRNAs at A, P, and E sites while corrected subunit-size values remain teacher enrichment

loci.title: Polypeptide Elongation Conveyor
loci.micro_anchor: the conveyor where codon recognition, peptide-bond growth, and translocation repeat to lengthen the polypeptide

loci.title: Stop and Release Dock
loci.micro_anchor: the termination dock where a stop codon ends translation, the product is released, and protein folding continues afterward

loci.title: Retroviral Reverse-Flow Gate
loci.micro_anchor: the exception gate where reverse transcriptase copies retroviral RNA into DNA before that DNA can integrate into a host genome

loci.title: Expression Control Room
loci.micro_anchor: the control room where regulatory DNA and proteins determine constitutive versus inducible output instead of treating every gene as always on

loci.title: Operon Architecture Board
loci.micro_anchor: the bacterial control board separating promoter, operator, structural genes, and repressor protein while showing coordinated operon regulation

loci.title: trp Repressible Chamber
loci.micro_anchor: the feedback chamber where tryptophan binds the repressor as a corepressor and switches a repressible operon toward lower transcription

loci.title: lac Inducible Chamber
loci.micro_anchor: the inducible chamber where allolactose changes repressor behavior and permits lac-operon transcription when the substrate signal is present

loci.title: Eukaryotic Regulation Layers
loci.micro_anchor: the layered control wall showing that eukaryotic gene expression can be coordinated at chromatin, transcriptional, RNA-processing, translational, and post-translational stages

loci.title: Epigenetic Chromatin Room
loci.micro_anchor: the chromatin room connecting reversible DNA/histone modifications with gene-expression state while keeping their effects context dependent

loci.title: Promoter–Enhancer Recruitment Hall
loci.micro_anchor: the regulatory hall where promoter and enhancer/control elements recruit transcription machinery from positions that may lie upstream, downstream, or within genes

loci.title: Activator–Repressor Balance Gate
loci.micro_anchor: the balance gate where positive and negative regulators change transcriptional output rather than simply labeling genes on or off

loci.title: RNA-Level Regulation Suite
loci.micro_anchor: the RNA regulation suite where alternative splicing and small RNAs such as miRNA/siRNA change which messages persist or are used

loci.title: Expression Profile Console
loci.micro_anchor: the console connecting gene-expression profiles and gene-product amount/function to phenotype

loci.title: Cell Specialization Gallery
loci.micro_anchor: the gallery where differential gene expression produces tissue-specific proteins and differentiated cell identities

loci.title: Developmental Sequence Hall
loci.micro_anchor: the developmental hall where sequential gene expression is linked with morphogenesis, cytoplasmic determinants, induction, pattern formation, homeotic genes, and apoptosis as teacher-enrichment mechanisms

loci.title: Mutation Consequence Desk
loci.micro_anchor: the triage desk where a DNA change is interpreted through its molecular consequence, environmental context, and possible connection from genotype to phenotype and selection

loci.title: Substitution Sorter
loci.micro_anchor: the sorter comparing point substitution outcomes including silent, missense, and nonsense changes without assuming every substitution has the same effect

loci.title: Frameshift Reading Track
loci.micro_anchor: the reading track where insertion/deletion changes the downstream reading frame when the net change is not a multiple of three

loci.title: Mutation Source and Variation Yard
loci.micro_anchor: the yard connecting replication errors and mutagens to random DNA change, then placing mutation alongside conserved reproductive processes as sources of variation

loci.title: Chromosome Number Error Bay
loci.micro_anchor: the bay where cell-division errors such as nondisjunction alter chromosome number and can disrupt phenotype or development

loci.title: Chromosome Rearrangement Garage
loci.micro_anchor: the garage sorting deletion, duplication, inversion, and translocation as structural chromosome alterations

loci.title: Horizontal Gene Transfer Hub
loci.micro_anchor: the microbial transfer hub distinguishing transformation, transduction, and conjugation as routes of horizontal gene transfer

loci.title: Mobile DNA and Viral Recombination Yard
loci.micro_anchor: the yard where transposable elements move within genomes and coinfecting viruses can recombine genetic material

loci.title: Genetic Engineering Intake
loci.micro_anchor: the laboratory intake defining genetic engineering as purposeful manipulation or analysis of nucleic acids before individual techniques are chosen

loci.title: Gel Electrophoresis Lane
loci.micro_anchor: the gel lane where charged DNA fragments migrate through a matrix and produce band patterns used for comparison

loci.title: PCR Thermal Cycler
loci.micro_anchor: the thermal cycler repeating denaturation, primer annealing, and extension to amplify a selected DNA region

loci.title: Transformation Expression Bench
loci.micro_anchor: the bacterial bench connecting uptake of engineered DNA with recombinant expression while distinguishing laboratory transformation from natural HGT context

loci.title: Sequence and Profile Analysis Desk
loci.micro_anchor: the analysis desk where DNA sequencing determines nucleotide order and DNA profiles compare patterns among samples

scope_guards.canonical_statement: For the AP Exam, names of replication steps and particular enzymes beyond DNA polymerase, ligase, RNA polymerase, helicase, and topoisomerase are outside required scope.
Details and names of enzymes and factors involved in translation steps are outside AP Exam scope.
Memorization of the genetic code is outside AP Exam scope except for the start codon AUG; students should use a supplied code chart.
Specific named mutations and their detailed effects are beyond AP Exam scope unless provided in a question context.
Specific disorders caused by chromosome-number changes are beyond AP Exam scope unless supplied in context.
Detailed procedural knowledge of gel electrophoresis, PCR, bacterial transformation, and DNA sequencing is beyond AP Exam scope beyond the required functional principles.

Do not answer a generic “bond holding nucleotides together” prompt with hydrogen bonds. Phosphodiester bonds link adjacent nucleotides within a strand; hydrogen bonds stabilize complementary base pairing between strands/regions.

scope_guards.canonical_label: Typical DNA/RNA structure is not absolute
scope_guards.canonical_statement: Treat double-stranded DNA and single-stranded RNA as typical cellular patterns, not universal rules across all nucleic acids and viruses.

scope_guards.canonical_label: Extra replication enzyme names are enrichment
scope_guards.canonical_statement: SSBPs, primase, DNA polymerase I/III, and detailed primer-removal machinery are scientifically useful teacher enrichment but are not current AP-required enzyme-name targets.
Telomeres/telomerase are valid biology but are outside the current Unit 6 AP-required replication content.

scope_guards.canonical_label: Transcription location depends on cell type
scope_guards.canonical_statement: Do not encode “transcription occurs in the nucleus” as universal; that statement applies to eukaryotic nuclear genes, while prokaryotes transcribe DNA without a nucleus.

scope_guards.canonical_label: TATA box is not every eukaryotic promoter
scope_guards.canonical_statement: Do not equate “eukaryotic promoter” with “TATA box.” TATA is one promoter element found in some genes.

scope_guards.canonical_label: Exon does not mean entirely protein-coding
scope_guards.canonical_statement: Do not define exons simply as amino-acid-coding sequence; mature transcripts can retain noncoding exon regions such as UTRs.
Use near universality, not absolute universality, when connecting the genetic code to common ancestry.

scope_guards.canonical_label: Ribosome size values are enrichment and corrected
scope_guards.canonical_statement: Do not use the slide’s 30S/40S prokaryotic pair. If ribosomal S values are retained as enrichment, use bacterial 30S + 50S and eukaryotic cytosolic 40S + 60S.

scope_guards.canonical_label: Retroviral DNA integrates into host DNA
scope_guards.canonical_statement: Do not encode the slide phrase that reverse-transcribed DNA becomes part of RNA. It can integrate into host genomic DNA.

scope_guards.canonical_label: trp repressor is not an enzyme
scope_guards.canonical_statement: Do not encode the trp repressor as an allosteric enzyme. It is a regulatory protein activated by the corepressor tryptophan.

scope_guards.canonical_label: lac operon is not a human lactase pathway
scope_guards.canonical_statement: Do not teach the lac operon as simply producing lactase. Its structural genes encode bacterial proteins including β-galactosidase and lactose permease.
Avoid universal claims that methylation always condenses DNA or that twin disease discordance is simply “inherited epigenetics.” Preserve reversible gene-regulatory effects with appropriate context.

Morphogenesis, cytoplasmic determinants, homeotic genes, and apoptosis are teacher enrichment; the current AP-required core is regulation, transcription-factor effects, differential expression, and specialization.

scope_guards.canonical_label: Frameshift effects are not universally catastrophic
scope_guards.canonical_statement: Insertion/deletion frameshifts can strongly alter downstream coding sequence, but effects vary and in-frame indels do not shift the frame.
Named disorders such as trisomy 21 remain contextual enrichment because the current CED excludes specific chromosome-number disorders as required knowledge.
Use aneuploidy for gain/loss of individual chromosomes and polyploidy/triploidy for extra whole chromosome sets; do not merge these categories.

scope_guards.canonical_label: Selection acts on heritable phenotypic variation
scope_guards.canonical_statement: Do not imply every mutation is directly selected. Selection changes frequencies of heritable variants when their phenotypic effects influence reproductive success in context.
Teach what gel electrophoresis, PCR, bacterial transformation, and sequencing accomplish and how to interpret results; do not require unnecessary procedural details beyond current CED scope.
